sheet-1-1.description: Sheet 1 shows six blocks in the north-eastern part of Perth Amboy, in the district drawn around Easton and Huntington Streets. The sheet is bounded by the double-track railroad on the left, lettered C.R.R. of N.J., and Charles Street on the right, with Easton running across the middle and Huntington Street across the bottom. Catherine and Cortlandt Streets cross both. The three upper blocks (numbers 274, 275 and 276) are cut off along a slanting line at the top, where a dashed 6-inch water pipe marks the edge of the drawn area, and they hold rows of frame dwellings with a few brick and hollow tile dwellings, a barn, a bottling works and two saloons. The lower blocks (273, 272 and 271) are more closely built. Block 272 carries the Church of Our Lady of Hungary, heated by steam and lit by electricity, with its rectory beside it; block 271 has Public School No. 5, a large brick building with steam heat and electric light, and a bake house; block 273 holds the North Amboy Coal Company yard with a gasoline tank, flats, a saloon and rows of frame dwellings along Catherine Street. House numbers are printed along the street frontages, with 6-inch water pipes and hydrants in the streets. A compass rose stands in the blank area at the upper left, outside the mapped streets, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The inset at the lower left, a separate piece of New Brunswick Avenue, is mapped as part 2.
notes: Easton is today's Wayne Street; Catherine, Cortlandt, Charles and Huntington keep their names as Catherine Street, Cortlandt Street, Charles Street and Huntington Street.
The sheet number carries a previous-edition reference (24) in the corner.
Easton/Huntington district NE; part 1 main, part 2 inset New Brunswick Av at Mitchell/Packer (two hand-picked points, anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-1-2.description: This inset at the lower left of sheet 1 shows a short stretch of New Brunswick Avenue in the western part of Perth Amboy, drawn at its own orientation inside a heavy-ruled box and separate from the street grid of the main sheet. New Brunswick Avenue runs the full height of the box as a 66-foot street with an 8-inch water pipe in it, and Mitchell Street and Packer Street are lettered where they meet it from the west, one near the upper end of the box and one near the lower end. East of the avenue lie two blocks, numbers 195 and 196, which are mostly open ground with a handful of buildings: a few frame dwellings and sheds, a small brick building, a shed with a cross mark, and a fire hydrant. The box has its own north arrow, pointing to the upper right, which shows how far the inset is turned from the main part of the sheet. Part of the left side of the box is cut by the border where the two cross streets enter. Scale is 50 feet to an inch, the same as the main part of the sheet.
notes: Mitchell Street and Packer Street are today's Mitchell Place and Packer Place; New Brunswick Avenue keeps its name.

Placed from the two street mouths where Mitchell and Packer Streets meet New Brunswick Avenue, read at the heavy border of the box, with scale from the main part of the sheet and rotation from the street direction; low confidence.
Easton/Huntington district NE; part 1 main, part 2 inset New Brunswick Av at Mitchell/Packer (two hand-picked points, anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the north-eastern edge of the old city where State Street bends north-west past the railroad. State Street runs diagonally up the middle of the sheet as a wide street, with the double-track railroad lettered P. R. R. along its west side. East of State Street, small blocks (216 to 220) lie between Chauncey, Lynd, Wayne and James Streets, and Parker Street runs along the right-hand edge of the drawn area. West of the railroad, Easton and Huntington Streets cross Charles and Elizabeth Streets in a more regular grid of blocks 220, 269 and 277, and the narrow blocks along the west side of State Street (block 340) are drawn on a slant. Most of the buildings are frame dwellings, with tenements, saloons and halls along State Street and its corners. The Ruthenian Greek Catholic Church of the Assumption of the Holy Virgin, with its rectory, stands on the west side; a Hall stands at the top above Chauncey Street. On block 218 is the fire department building, with Liberty Truck Company No. 2 and fire alarm boxes marked at the corner of Wayne Street. Six-inch and larger water pipes run in every street, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at the corners. Compass rose and scale bar are at the right, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The corner carries previous-edition sheet numbers 24 and 25.
notes: Easton, west of State Street, and Wayne, east of it, are the same street, today's Wayne Street.
State Street here is today's State Street; the railroad along it is the line shown by OpenStreetMap as the North Jersey Coast Line.
State Street bend, Chauncey/Lynd/Wayne/James. 50 ft. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the north-western edge of the built-up city, where Brace Avenue crosses the district of Cleveland Avenue and Donald Avenue. Brace Avenue is the wide diagonal street across the middle of the sheet, and Compton Avenue and Neville Street run across the lower third. Cleveland Avenue and Convery Place form one street running down the left side, with Pacific Avenue on the right and Donald Avenue between, and Kennedy Street, Love Lane and Hall Avenue crossing the upper blocks. Harrington is lettered along the top-left edge and Mary at the top right. The upper blocks (312C to 312L and 313C) are large tracts divided into long narrow lots, built up only along the street frontages with frame dwellings, a few hollow tile and concrete block houses; Love Lane cuts through the block between Donald and Pacific Avenues. The lower blocks (244A, 244B, 246B and 246C) are almost empty except for Public School No. 8, a brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, set in block 244B on Compton Avenue, with four frame dwellings beside it. A fire alarm box is marked at the junction of Brace Avenue and Convery Place. The compass rose is at the left, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets 4 and 9 are numbered at the right and bottom.
notes: Cleveland Avenue and Convery Place together are today's Convery Boulevard.
Love Lane appears to be the stretch of today's Hall Avenue between Donald and Pacific Avenues.
Convery Boulevard and Kennedy Street meet 3 m off the drawn junction and were left out of the fit.
Brace/Compton/Neville with Convery Boulevard (printed Cleveland Av / Convery Pl); rotation -20.9. 50 ft.

sheet-4-1.description: Sheet 4 covers the western edge of the city in the district of Pacific, Atlantic and Cornell Streets. Three north-south streets, Pacific Avenue, Atlantic Avenue and Cornell, cross Hall Avenue at the top, Brace Avenue in the middle, with Compton Avenue and Neville running across the lower third; Groom is lettered below Brace Avenue. In the upper right, Amboy Avenue, also lettered as Woodbridge Road, runs diagonally down to the right, with Arnold Avenue above it and Jeffreys Street at the right edge. The upper blocks (311A to 311E) are large tracts divided into long narrow lots, built only along the street frontages with frame dwellings, a few hollow tile houses and a milk house. At Amboy Avenue and Hall Avenue stands the Garfield Engine Company No. 5 fire house, with a note of its steam engine, combination wagon, chemical tanks and volunteer members. Blocks 247 and 248 below Brace Avenue are drawn as slanting blocks with dwellings, an embroidery shop and a hollow tile construction shop. Six-inch water pipes with hydrants run in the streets, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The lower right corner, below a heavy line, is a separate inset at another place and is mapped as part 2; the sheet numbers 5, 10 and 0 around the edges name the adjoining sheets.
notes: Jeffreys Street is today's Jeffries Street.
Groom and Brace Avenue meet 30 m east of Pacific Avenue today; the drawn Groom junctions were 14 to 16 m off the detected position and were not used.
Amboy Avenue is also lettered Woodbridge Road on the sheet.
Pacific/Atlantic/Cornell district; part 2 inset Ostergaard Tile Works at Sayre Av (one hand-picked point, anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-4-2.description: This inset in the lower right corner of sheet 4, enclosed by heavy rules, shows the Ostergaard Tile Works on Sayre Avenue in the western part of Perth Amboy, at a different location from the rest of the sheet. Sayre Avenue runs down the left of the inset as a 60-foot street tilted from the vertical, and Packer Street enters it from the east about halfway down. The works, lettered Ostergaard Tile Works, Floor Tiling, fills most of the inset; it consists of brick and frame buildings arranged round a kiln room with three round kilns, with a press room, drying room, mixing room, bins, stock rooms, a heater and electric motor room, and a machine shop, with a private railroad spur curving in from the lower right. A note beside it lists the works' night watchman and clock stations, fire pails and extinguishers, electric power with seven motors and steam heat. A storage building and iron building stand by the works, and across Sayre Avenue are a hollow tile warehouse and a hollow tile and cement warehouse, a small office, and a line of lots at the right edge (187B and 187C), with a fire hydrant on the avenue. The inset is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned about 45 degrees from the main part of the sheet.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point at the junction of Sayre Avenue and Packer Street, with scale taken from the main part of the sheet and rotation from the direction of Sayre Avenue; low confidence.
Packer Street is today's Packer Place; Sayre Avenue keeps its name.
Pacific/Atlantic/Cornell district; part 2 inset Ostergaard Tile Works at Sayre Av (one hand-picked point, anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the district around the junction of Amboy Avenue with Hall Avenue in the western part of the city. Amboy Avenue, also lettered Woodbridge Road, runs diagonally from the upper left to the bottom of the sheet, and Hall Avenue, Jeffreys, Ridgeley and Sutton cross the right-hand blocks. Arnold Avenue runs along the top, Alta Vista Place runs down between the upper blocks, and Jaques is the north-south street at the right edge. At the lower left, Brace Avenue, Compton Avenue and Neville cross the left-hand blocks, with Cornell at the edge. The upper blocks (290, 291 and 292) are large with long narrow lots, built up mainly along Hall Avenue with frame dwellings, a casino, a brick building and a few outbuildings, while blocks 283 and 282 on the east side hold a few dwellings and a hollow tile works. Blocks 249 and 250 below Amboy Avenue are drawn as slanting blocks with frame and brick dwellings, and a few more buildings at the corner of Compton Avenue. A fire alarm box is marked near Hall Avenue. Six-inch and 12-inch water pipes run in the streets, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its scale bar at the bottom left. The compass rose is at the left. Adjoining sheets 4, 6 and 11 are numbered.
notes: Jaques is today's Jacques Street and Jeffreys is today's Jeffries Street.
The right-hand street, Jaques, is cut by the sheet edge; its junctions were placed from the drawn edge.
Amboy Av (Woodbridge Rd) at Hall Av. 50 ft.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows a regular grid of ten blocks in the western part of Perth Amboy, between Meredith and Sutton from top to bottom and between Jaques and Penn from left to right, with Johnstone running down the middle. Meredith runs along the top edge, with Arnold Avenue, Hall Avenue, Jeffreys, Ridgeley and Sutton crossing the sheet at regular intervals below it; Arnold Avenue is noted as 60 feet wide. Johnstone is drawn as a slightly slanting street, so the blocks on either side of it have one side cut at an angle, while Jaques and Penn are straight. The blocks (numbers 280 to 289, 293, 294, 297 and 298) are large with long narrow lots, and only the lots along the north-south streets are built, mostly with frame dwellings. East of Johnstone, block 288 holds an embroidery shop and a hollow tile house, block 294 a hall, and block 280 near the bottom right another hall. Most of the west half is open ground. Six-inch and 12-inch water pipes run in the streets, with hydrants at corners and the street widths marked as 60 feet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the scale bar at the lower right, and the compass rose stands on the right edge. Adjoining sheets 5, 7, 11 and 12 are numbered at the edges, and the corner carries sheet numbers 28 and 29 of the previous edition.
notes: Jaques is today's Jacques Street and Jeffreys is today's Jeffries Street.
Meredith and Sutton lie on the edges of the sheet, so their junctions were placed from the one drawn edge.
Regular grid Meredith-Sutton by Jaques-Penn. 50 ft.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers part of the west side of Perth Amboy, between Meredith Street at the top and Sutton Street at the bottom, and from Penn Street at the left to Cortlandt Street at the right. Hall Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right. West Side Avenue runs down the sheet to the south of Hall Avenue, and the double-track Central Railroad of New Jersey runs north and south through the middle, crossing Hall Avenue between the two. West of the railroad the blocks are lined with frame dwellings, with a saloon and hall on Meredith Street and a row of tenements facing Hall Avenue, and the ground north of Hall Avenue between West Side Avenue and the railroad is blank. East of the railroad, Catherine Street and Cortlandt Street divide the blocks. North of Hall Avenue are dwellings, a block of tenements along Huntington Street, a bakery, the coal and wood yard of Jos. Koval, and a hall with a saloon. South of Hall Avenue the lower right of the sheet is occupied by The New Jersey Terra Cotta Co., manufacturers of architectural terra cotta, whose pressing, modelling and fitting sheds, laboratory, clay mills, kilns and storage tanks fill most of the blocks beside the railroad. The New Jersey Portland Cement Co. is named at the bottom edge. Block numbers are lettered in the middle of each block. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants at the corners. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale bar along the bottom edge.
notes: Jeffreys Street is Jeffries Street today.
Hall Avenue east of West Side Avenue is carried in OpenStreetMap under the name Hall Avenue Honorary Avenida Puerto Rico.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey is drawn about 12 m from the line of the modern North Jersey Coast Line when fitted through the streets.
A Library of Congress duplicate stamp is printed at the top left.
Hall Av / West Side Av / Cortlandt; N.J. Terra Cotta Co.; Central R.R. drawn 12 m from its modern line. 50 ft.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 lies east of sheet 7 in the west side of Perth Amboy and is bounded by Huntington Street at the top, Hall Avenue across the middle, and by Cortlandt Street at the left and State Street at the right; James Street meets State Street at the top right corner. Charles Street and Elizabeth Street run down the sheet between them. The blocks north of Hall Avenue are mostly dwellings with some small shops, and Kellner Bros. sausage factory with its hollow tile and brick buildings at the top of the Charles Street block, next to the Polish National Church. South of Hall Avenue the blocks are narrow dwelling lots running down to the lower edge of the sheet, with a saloon, motion picture premises and a bakery fronting Hall Avenue and a synagogue and an auto shop in the lower blocks. A railroad crosses the sheet diagonally and Hall Avenue at about the middle of its right half, and a Lehigh Valley railroad swings in a curve across the lower right corner, where a signal tower is drawn. The Office of Lehigh Valley Transit Co. stands on the right edge near the top. The blocks in the upper right between the railroad and State Street are filled with a row of narrow frame dwellings. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale bar along the bottom edge, and shows 6 inch and larger water pipes in the streets.
notes: Hall Avenue east of West Side Avenue is carried in OpenStreetMap under the name Hall Avenue Honorary Avenida Puerto Rico.
Hall Avenue is lettered Hall Av. on the sheet.
The Library of Congress triplicate stamp is printed over the top right corner.
Huntington to Hall Av, Cortlandt to State; Lehigh Valley R.R. bottom right. 50 ft.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows a district in the northwest of the old city of Perth Amboy, between Neville Street at the top and Sayre Avenue across the bottom, and from Convery Place at the left to Groom Street at the right. New Brunswick Avenue runs diagonally across the middle of the sheet from upper left to lower right. The upper third is a large area of platted but unbuilt lots between Neville Street and Lawrie Street, with the hospital grounds below it. The Perth Amboy City Hospital, drawn with its administration building, east and west wards, and a nurses' home, stands on the north side of New Brunswick Avenue facing a row of dwellings on Lawrie Street. South of New Brunswick Avenue are the short blocks between Convery Place, Baker Place, Steadman Place, Broadhead Place and Lawton Place, built with frame dwellings, two tenements, a few small shops and sheds, a blacksmith shop and a hollow tile house. Sayre Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet and has long narrow lots along its south side, many still empty. The right margin carries a north arrow and compass rose, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale bar at the lower left. Block numbers 245, 242, 186 and 385 are lettered on the blocks, and water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are drawn along the streets with hydrants and telephone points at the corners.
notes: Convery Place is drawn here in the position of the modern Convery Boulevard, which fits the sheet within about 1 m at its junctions.
Lawton Place at New Brunswick Avenue was 15 m from its modern node and was left out of the fit.
A Library of Congress triplicate stamp is printed at the top left.
Hospital; Convery/Baker/Steadman/Broadhead/Lawton Places; turned about -20. 50 ft.

sheet-10-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 10 is the main map, covering ground to the east of sheet 9 between Neville Street at the top and Sayre Avenue at the bottom, and from Groom Street on the left to Cornell Street on the right. The upper two thirds is a set of very large blocks between Neville, Lawrie and Barclay Streets, mostly unbuilt, with only two dwellings and a few sheds drawn in the block numbered 239 and nothing at all in block 240. New Brunswick Avenue crosses the left half of the sheet from the upper left towards the middle and Washington Avenue crosses the middle of the lower part, with Seaman Avenue running parallel below it. The built part is along those avenues: the Perth Amboy Foundry and Machine Co., with its cupola, machine shop and pattern shop, stands on the north side of Washington Avenue, and below the avenues are blocks of dwellings between Lawton Place and Mattano Place, a carpenter's, a tin shop, a cooper shop, Max Shapiro's barrel storage and a wholesale liquor store. Sayre Avenue crosses the bottom left corner. The inset at the top right, drawn inside a heavy line, is a separate part. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale bar at the bottom, and water pipes of 6, 8, 12 and 20 inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: The inset at the top right (Seaman Avenue, McCoy's Iron Works, Carl Christensen cement block shop) is not part of this reading; it is not georeferenced.
Washington Avenue here is Washington Street in OpenStreetMap, and its junction with New Brunswick Avenue was not detected.
Mattano Place does not appear in the modern street data.
The part carries a note (31), a reference to the adjoining sheet.
Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset top right (Seaman Av, McCoy Iron Works), not placed. 50 ft.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Seaman Avenue with McCoy Iron Works (no street junction; needs step 6b carried points from sheet 31).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 is turned about 70 degrees from the usual orientation of the sheets, so that west is at the top and the lettering of the vertical streets reads upward. It covers the blocks between Johnstone Street along the bottom edge and Cornell Street at the top, and from Washington Street at the left to Sutton Street at the right. Barclay, Lawrie and Neville Streets cross the sheet from top to bottom and Amboy Avenue, also lettered Woodbridge Road, passes diagonally across the middle. Jaques Street meets Neville and Sutton Streets near the lower right. The blocks are mostly lined with frame dwellings with small outbuildings and brick pits, many lots still open, a junk dealer on Washington Street, a stone cutter's, a carpenter shop and a bakery with ovens. Wm. Struve and Sons, florists, occupy the middle of the sheet south of Amboy Avenue, with a large green house and a work room heated by hot water. A Danish Seventh Day Adventist church stands at the top of the block east of Neville Street. The lower right corner is filled by the Perth Amboy Cigar Co., a branch of the United Cigar Manufacturers Co., a brick cigar factory with sweating, stripping and packing floors and a drying warehouse, and its description is printed in the right margin. A north arrow is drawn at the top left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Jaques Street is Jacques Street today.
The Amboy Avenue stretches side by side in OpenStreetMap were checked; the junctions on the main line fit within 1.2 m.
The sheet is turned so that north points to the right, with a rotation of about 70 degrees from the standard sheet.
Compton Avenue is lettered Compton Av. at the right edge.
Turned (rotation about +70); Amboy Av / Woodbridge Rd; cigar factory. 50 ft.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers a block of the west side of Perth Amboy between Sutton Street at the top and Washington Street at the bottom, and from Johnstone Street at the left to West Side Avenue at the right, with Penn Street running down the middle of the right half. Neville, Lawrie and Barclay Streets cross the sheet. The upper blocks between Sutton and Neville Streets are lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots at the left and right with a large open block between, and the blocks below it are similar, with some open lots. Institutions stand in the lower blocks: Public School No. 6, a large brick building heated by steam, stands west of Johnstone Street at the left, the Church of Our Lady of the Holy Rosary, a Roman Catholic church with its rectory, stands on Washington Street, and Holy Cross Episcopal Church is a small building at the lower left. East of Penn Street the Holy Trinity Roman Catholic Church and its rectory occupy the upper block near West Side Avenue, and a row of narrow brick houses with a hollow tile house stands on Penn Street. The right margin carries a compass rose and the railroad of the Central Railroad of New Jersey and the Lehigh Valley railroad run at the right edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale bar at the bottom.
notes: The railroad corridor at the right edge is drawn about 24 m from the modern line when fitted through the streets, so the mask stops before it; it is shown on sheet 13.
A Library of Congress triplicate stamp is printed at the top right.
Sutton to Washington, Johnstone to West Side Av; rail corridor at right masked out (drawn 24 m off). 50 ft.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the railroad corridor and the ground east of it in the west side of Perth Amboy, with Washington Street across the bottom and William Street across the lower middle, between Park Avenue and Division Street at the right. A wide bundle of main-line tracks of the Pennsylvania and Central railroads runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs down the left edge. The large area west of the tracks is blank. In the upper part of the sheet are the works of The New Jersey Portland Cement Co., with its cement mill, kilns, dryer, steel frame storage and an office and laboratory, and its sidings, and at the extreme upper left the fitting shed of The New Jersey Terra Cotta Co. At the lower left Potts and Kaufman, wholesale grocery, occupy a brick warehouse beside the tracks, with a row of dwellings along Washington Street. East of the tracks, the blocks between Park Avenue and Division Street hold dwellings, an ice house and the Perth Amboy Coal and Ice Co., with sheds, and F. Huda, wagon builder, with a lumber shed and blacksmith shop. East Av. is lettered along the bottom edge. The compass rose stands in the middle of the blank area. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Four control points only; two measured on streets with residuals of 2 to 4 m and one on a railroad crossing, so the placement is low confidence.
The wide bundle of main-line tracks drawn on this sheet was not used as control.
Rail corridor and cement works; only 4 control points (one a rail crossing); low. 50 ft.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows a belt of mixed industrial and residential blocks in Perth Amboy lying either side of the Pennsylvania Railroad, between Washington Street at the bottom and Gold Street at the top, with Division Street on the left and State Street on the right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned about 20 degrees, so the streets run up and down the page. The railroad crosses the sheet from top to bottom, widening into a fan of tracks and yards at the upper left. Beside it on the west is the yard of the Perth Amboy Supply Company, dealers in masons' materials and coal, with coal bins, a sand shed, a cement storage house and sheds. South of William Street the Thomas Langan Lumber Company occupies the blocks between the tracks and State Street, with lumber sheds, lumber forms and a lime, cement and plaster house. Public School No. 2 stands on the State Street block south of the lumber yard, a large brick building heated by hot air and hot water. The remaining blocks are built up with frame dwellings in rows, a terrace of brick houses and shops on the east side of Miller Street near William Street, a tenement building, an undertaker's and hollow-tile structures along State Street near Buckingham Avenue. Water mains of four, six, eight and twelve inches are shown in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The right-hand part of the sheet above Buckingham Avenue is left blank, being drawn on a neighbouring sheet. A compass rose at the left shows the turned orientation. Block numbers 202 to 208, 223 and 257 are printed, and neighbouring sheets 8, 13, 15, 20 and 30 are indicated at the margins.
notes: De Kalb Avenue is Dekalb Avenue today.
Gold Street is not in the modern street data.
Miller Street is drawn 30 feet wide against the wider modern right-of-way; its junction with William Street has the largest residual of the sheet (3 m).
Printed scale bar: 50 feet to an inch.
State/Division/Washington, Pennsylvania R.R. across; Miller St drawn 30 ft. 50 ft.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the industrial centre of the old Perth Amboy waterfront district between State Street on the left and High Street on the right, from Buckingham Avenue at the top to Washington Street at the bottom, with Mechanic Street and De Kalb Avenue crossing the middle. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees, so that the streets run up and down the sheet. The upper right quarter is occupied by the Perth Amboy Chemical Works of the Roessler and Hasslacher Chemical Company: Plant No. 2, manufacturers of cyanide, with a formaldehyde house, alcohol refinery, recovery rooms, charcoal furnaces and storage, ammonia drying towers and tanks, engine and generator rooms, a store house, coal shed and conveyor, and a turntable, with a note on its fire protection at the head of the sheet. A railroad track and sidings with storage tanks run along High Street on the right edge. South of De Kalb Avenue the Standard Underground Cable Company occupies the block between Mechanic and High Streets, a large rubber mill drawn from plans, with a cigar factory and dwellings along Mechanic Street. West of Mechanic Street the upper blocks are church property: St. Stephen's Roman Catholic Church, its rectory and a convent stand in large lots, with rows of dwellings below. Between De Kalb Avenue and Washington Street the blocks hold stores, flats, photographers' studios, a saloon, factories and dwellings. Hydrants, fire alarm boxes and water mains of four to twelve inches are shown. Block numbers 200 to 207 are printed and neighbouring sheets 14, 16, 20, 21 and 30 are named in the margins.
notes: De Kalb Avenue is Dekalb Avenue today.
The Roessler and Hasslacher plant carries a note 'See Note in Margin'.
Mechanic Street, Washington Street and High Street are drawn narrower between edges than the 66 foot printed width.
Roessler & Hasslacher Plant 2, Standard Underground Cable. 50 ft.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows the waterfront industrial strip of Perth Amboy east of High Street, from Buckingham Avenue at the top to Washington Street at the bottom, out to Staten Island Sound on the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees. The upper half is the Atlantic Terra Cotta Company, Plant No. 2, a large works of pink brick and yellow frame buildings for clay mixing, pressing, glazing, kilns, spraying, drying and fitting, with circular kilns, coal and clay storage, a track on trestle and a coal trestle running out to the water, and a fire protection note at the head of the sheet. Below it, a timber yard and the works of the Raritan Dry Dock Company occupy the shore, with floating dry docks numbered 1 to 3 (500, 1,500 and 3,500 tons), marine railways, piers on piles, a saw mill and carpenter shop, boiler shop, machine shop, oil and paint storage and the Standard Oil Company's tanks. The lower left is taken by the Standard Underground Cable Company's large mill for electrical wires and cables, with machine shop, rolling mill, wire mill, cable department and shipping buildings, and a side track from the main line. High Street runs up the left edge, where only part of the street is shown. The shore of Staten Island Sound is drawn with piers and docks, and the bottom of the sheet shows the heads of Rector and Front Streets south of Washington Street.
notes: Hartford Street is lettered above Buckingham Avenue near the top edge; Rector Street and Front Street appear only as street names south of Washington Street.
High Street is 99 feet wide and only its east half is on the sheet, so the High and Washington Street junction is held out of the fit.
Atlantic Terra Cotta Plant 2, Raritan Dry Dock, Staten Island Sound; 4 points; High/Washington excluded (High half on sheet). 50 ft.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the area in the north-west of old Perth Amboy where New Brunswick Avenue and Amboy Avenue (Woodbridge Road) meet, with the Lehigh Valley Railroad yards filling the middle of the sheet. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 70 degrees, so that Washington Street runs up the right edge and Lehigh Avenue down the left. The left strip is entirely industrial: Ford's Porcelain Works, Plant No. 2, the New Jersey Wood Finishing Company (varnish manufacturers) and the Atlantic Terra Cotta Company, Plant No. 4, with kilns, pressing and modelling shops, storage sheds and pug mills. A broad fan of tracks of the Lehigh Valley Railroad occupies the centre, with a passenger depot and the coal and wood yard of Henry W. Kinsey beside it. To the right, between the tracks and Washington Street, New Brunswick Avenue runs diagonally and carries rows of frame dwellings, with Seaman Avenue, Ogden Place and Kinsey Place cutting across the blocks, and stores, a hotel (the Eagle Hotel) and a dairy near the Amboy Avenue crossing. Hotel Dania stands on the south side of Amboy Avenue, among bakeries, a bottling shop, saloons and dwellings. Johnstone Street closes the sheet at the bottom right and Stanford Street at the bottom left. Block numbers 105 to 114 are printed with neighbouring sheets 0, 10, 11, 18, 23 and 24 at the margins.
notes: Amboy Avenue is lettered 'Amboy Av. (Woodbridge Rd.)'.
Kinsey Place is not in the modern street data.
Stockton Street and Gifford Street are shown only at the left edge; the Lehigh Avenue and Stockton Street junction lies just off the sheet and was not detected.
Seaman Avenue, Ogden Place and the Seaman and Ogden junction are in the fit; Ogden Place and Seaman Avenue survive today.
New Brunswick / Amboy Av, Lehigh Valley yards, turned +70. 50 ft.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows the railroad corridor of Perth Amboy south of Amboy Avenue, where the Lehigh Valley Railroad and the Central Railroad of New Jersey converge, with Washington Street along the right edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 70 degrees, so Washington Street runs up the page. A great fan of tracks narrowing towards the top fills the middle of the sheet, with the lumber yard of I. R. Robbins, the coal and wood yard of J. W. Obuch, a freight house and a feed warehouse. The Central Railroad of New Jersey main line crosses the lower part of the sheet from side to side, with a siding serving A. M. Metzendorf's flour and grain warehouse and a baled hay and straw warehouse. At the top left, beside Lehigh Avenue, Frankel and Markoff's coal and ice yard, an ice house and rows of frame dwellings stand between Stanford Street and Prospect Street. At the top right are the Raritan Cement Stone and Contracting Company's cement block shop and a contractors' yard. A row of dwellings and small stores lines the east side of the tracks along Washington Street. New Brunswick Avenue runs diagonally across the left half with Oak Street and Elm Street entering it, and the bottom strip shows blocks of dwellings, a pickle works, a wagon shed and a beer depot along East Avenue. Block numbers 90, 102 to 104 and 119 are printed and neighbouring sheets are named at the margins.
notes: The printed label 'East 19 Av.' is East Avenue with sheet number 19 overprinted.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line is drawn about 21 m from its modern line against the streets; the railroad crossings are not used as strong control.
The sheet fits at 7.77 px/ft, about 3 percent below the 50 foot scan constant of other sheets.
Rail corridor, turned +70; Central R.R. drawn 21 m off. 50 ft.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows a residential and light industrial part of Perth Amboy west of Division Street and south of Washington Street, in four blocks across and three down. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees. Washington Street runs along the top, Broad Street crosses the upper part and Barracks Street the lower, with East Avenue on the left, Park Avenue near the centre and Division Street on the right; New Brunswick Avenue crosses the bottom diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, with Maple Street and Madison Avenue at the lower edge. The blocks along Washington and Broad Streets are mainly rows of frame dwellings and flats, with John H. Sloan's embroidery shop and the Perth Amboy Manufacturing Company, makers of waists and dresses, among them. The middle block between Broad and Barracks Streets holds the public school group, a Grammar School and a Manual Training School with a boiler house, with dwellings along its Park Avenue and Division Street fronts. South of Barracks Street are the Katz Brothers shirt factory, the Wilentz Company cigar and tobacco factory, H. Rippen's cigar factory and tobacco factory, a bale hay storehouse and dwellings, packed along New Brunswick Avenue. Division Street jogs sideways at Broad Street. Water mains and hydrants are shown. Block numbers 91 to 94, 100 and 101 are printed, with neighbouring sheets 13, 18, 20 and 26 named at the margins.
notes: Division Street is drawn with an offset at Broad Street; both modern Broad and Division junctions are used.
The street lettered 'New' between Barracks Street and New Brunswick Avenue is New Street today.
The sheet fits at 7.82 px/ft, about 2 percent below the 50 foot scan constant of other sheets.
Park Av / Division blocks, schools. 50 ft.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows the middle of Perth Amboy's old business district, where the Central Railroad of New Jersey and its passenger depot cut north to south across the sheet, with State Street at the centre-right and Division Street at the left. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees. Washington Street runs along the top, Broad Street across the upper part, Commerce and Center Streets across the middle and Fayette Street along the bottom. The railroad station block holds the passenger depot, a turntable with an engine house, a freight house and tracks, and west of them is a long block between Division Street and the tracks with the Greek Catholic Church and Sunday school, storage and beer storehouses, a tenement and the Perth Amboy Beef Company. East of the tracks, along State Street, the shop fronts of the commercial block include Columbia Hall, the Perth Amboy Knitting Mills, a garage and many stores and saloons. The blocks east of State Street contain St. Stephen's Danish Evangelical Lutheran Church, St. Mary's Roman Catholic Church and its rectory, a Parochial School, a first school hall, a convent and a printing and furniture trade, with Mechanic Street at the right edge. The Middlesex Cigar Company, Branch of United Cigar Manufacturers, stands at the top left. Division Street is drawn with a jog at Broad Street. Block numbers 32 to 37 and 95 to 99 are printed, with neighbouring sheets named at the margins.
notes: Division Street jogs sideways at Broad Street; both modern Broad and Division junctions are used.
Washington, Fayette and Division junctions are flagged narrow (edges 38 to 43 ft apart against 66 feet), with residuals under 1.6 m.
Downtown with depot, State St. 50 ft.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers six blocks of the old downtown of Perth Amboy east of the Central Railroad, between Washington Street at the top and Fayette Street at the bottom, and between Mechanic Street on the left and Rector Street on the right, with High Street running down the middle. Broad, Commerce and Center Streets cross the sheet from left to right. The blocks between Mechanic and High Streets are closely built with frame and brick dwellings, flats and small stores, with a few bakery ovens, sheds and auto garages in the yards, a stuccoed tenement on Broad Street, an electric printing shop on Commerce Street, and on Fayette Street the First Baptist Church, a chapel and a hay, grain and feed warehouse. East of High Street the upper block between Washington and Broad Streets is only partly built, with dwellings along High Street and a large open lot towards Rector Street. The two lower blocks east of High Street, between Commerce and Fayette Streets, belong to the Roessler and Hasslacher Chemical Company: Plant No. 3 for metal salts manufacture, an electric department and drafting room, Department R, an experimental laboratory, and the main technical office, all brick buildings with concrete floors set in otherwise open ground, with a small upholstering shop on High Street. Six-inch and larger water pipes are drawn in every street with hydrants at the corners. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a scale bar on Center Street at the left edge; block numbers and the numbers of the adjoining sheets 15, 16, 20, 22, 28 and 29 are printed in the margins and streets.
notes: The Roessler and Hasslacher Chemical Company occupies the blocks between Commerce, High, Fayette and Rector Streets.
Pilot sheet for the atlas: 14 detected junctions.
Street names are printed without suffixes; today they are Washington, Broad, Commerce, Center, Fayette, Mechanic, High and Rector Streets.
Downtown: Washington to Fayette, Mechanic to Rector; Broad, Commerce, Center; Roessler & Hasslacher Chemical Co. 50 ft. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the Perth Amboy waterfront between Washington Street at the top and Fayette Street at the bottom, from Rector Street on the left to the shore of Staten Island Sound on the right. Front Street runs down the sheet beside the works, with Broad and Commerce Streets crossing it from the left. The upper left blocks hold small dwellings and sheds, with the lumber storage and sail loft of the P.A.D.D. Co. beside Front Street. To the right of Front Street the Perth Amboy Dry Dock Co., shipwrights, caulkers, machinists and boiler makers, occupies the shore with its machine shop, saw mill, iron storage and four dry docks (Nos. 1 to 4) cut into the water, each set in a bulkhead outline. Below Broad Street the Roessler and Hasslacher Chemical Co. fills the block along Commerce Street as Plant No. 1, with color, platinum, tin oxide, perborate and bleaching, soda, hydrogen and chlorine departments in brick buildings, a dock shed and Wharf and Bulkhead No. 24 on the water side. South of Commerce Street the same company has a laboratory department, a gas producer building and storage tanks, followed by the General Bakelite Co. works, a storehouse, and at the foot of the sheet a new Bakelite factory built in 1913 of reinforced concrete. Several long notes describe night watchman and hose arrangements. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose at lower right and a scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Street names in the modern data match those printed (Front, Rector, Broad, Commerce, Washington, Fayette).
The shore line and piers shown here have been rebuilt; only the street junctions were used as control.
A new factory for the Bakelite company at the foot of the sheet is marked 'Built 1913'.
Waterfront: Dry Dock Co, Roessler & Hasslacher Plant 1. 50 ft.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 lies at the western end of the Perth Amboy built-up area, between Lehigh Avenue at the top right and Smith Street along the bottom. The long narrow wedge of Kirkland Place, a slanting street, runs from top to bottom on the left, with one row of lots on its west side and a deeper row on its east side, both of small frame dwellings, with a Hungarian church, a tenement, and a coal and wood yard (A. Chereek) near Smith Street. A wide curve of railroad track of the Raritan Terminal and Transportation Co. sweeps across the middle and right of the sheet, enclosing a large open tract (block 132) that is blank on the plan. At the bottom, along Smith Street, the blocks between Kirkland Place, Goodwin Street and Gifford Street contain a mix of stores, saloons, a wholesale liquor dealer with a beer bottling works, tenements built of hollow tile and small dwellings, while a block at lower right between Goodwin and Gifford Streets holds a tenement of hollow tile and more dwellings. Fayette Street appears only at the right, east of the railroad. Grace Street is drawn as a narrow street crossing below Smith Street, and Bertrand Avenue runs along the right edge. Water pipes of 4, 6, 12 and 24 inches are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch; a compass rose is at the top and a scale bar at the bottom right.
notes: Kirkland Place is a slanting street with no cross street in the area drawn; Fayette Street is not drawn across it.
Fayette Street and Goodwin Street are in the modern data as meeting, but the sheet does not draw that junction; it was excluded.
Kirkland Place wedge, Raritan Terminal R.R. curve; 5 points mostly on Smith. 50 ft.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 shows a grid of regular residential blocks in the west of Perth Amboy, between Lehigh Avenue at the top and Smith Street at the bottom, with Fayette Street crossing the middle. Gifford Street is at the left edge, Stockton Street, Chapman Street and Watson Avenue divide the blocks, Stanford Street runs north of Fayette Street, and Prospect Street is at the right edge, with Bertrand Avenue and Davidson Avenue appearing south of Smith Street. The blocks hold mainly frame dwellings, many with flats, and several rows of paired brick tenements in block 128 on Stockton Street. Block 127 at the bottom holds a row of stores and a saloon along Smith Street. Public School No. 4, a three-story brick building heated by hot air and steam and fitted with Eastman extinguishers, stands on Stockton Street near Smith Street. A railroad branch of the Raritan Terminal and Transportation Co. cuts diagonally across the lower left and curves down towards Smith Street. Other features include a hall, bottling shops, an auto garage, a hollow tile garage and a water power shop. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches are marked, with hydrants at the corners. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with a compass rose at the top and a scale bar at the bottom right.
notes: Chapman Street is not in the modern street data; it is not used as control.
Watson Avenue and Stanford Street meet Fayette Street about 15 m apart, offset across it.
Residential, School No. 4; Chapman St not in modern data. 50 ft.

sheet-25-1.description: Sheet 25, part 1, is the main map of the sheet and shows four columns of residential blocks in the west part of Perth Amboy, between New Brunswick Avenue at the top and Smith Street at the bottom, with Fayette Street across the middle. Prospect Street, Oak Street and Elm Street run down the sheet, and Lehigh Avenue is lettered along the left edge. The blocks are mostly small frame dwellings and flats, with rows of stores and tenements along New Brunswick Avenue at the top, a hall, a saloon with a pool room, and a number of sheds and carriage houses. In block 124 the Standard Bedding Co., makers of mattresses and bed springs, has a brick factory, and a livery with carriage houses and a harness shop occupies the same block near Smith Street. A rag sorting and baling plant and scrap metal yard (Amboy Waste Products Co.) is in block 120 at the upper left, with tenements of three stories. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs as a vertical line down the right side of the sheet; the area to its right, block 26, is left blank. A heavy-lined inset at the top right is mapped separately. The map is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with a compass rose below the inset and a scale bar at the lower right.
notes: The inset at the top right is mapped separately as part 2; the mask of this part stops at the left edge of the rail corridor.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at the right, lies 15 to 20 m from the modern North Jersey Coast Line; the corridor was left out of the mask.
Two parts: 1 main (rail corridor masked, drawn 15-21 m off); 2 inset top right New Brunswick Av at Prospect/Oak (anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-25-2.description: Sheet 25, part 2, is the heavy-lined inset at the top right of the sheet. It shows a short stretch of New Brunswick Avenue, which crosses the inset from upper left to lower right, with the blocks on its south side between Prospect Street on the left and Oak Street at the right edge. The row of lots along the avenue holds a saloon, stores with flats above and small frame dwellings, with block 120 behind them. Block 18 lies across the avenue to the north, left blank. The inset is lettered with its own block and house numbers. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the avenue.
notes: Placed from a single measured point, New Brunswick Avenue at Prospect Street, which lies at the top edge of the inset, with the scale taken from the sheet; low confidence.
New Brunswick Avenue and Oak Street, picked by hand, agree with the placement to about 3 m.
Two parts: 1 main (rail corridor masked, drawn 15-21 m off); 2 inset top right New Brunswick Av at Prospect/Oak (anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the central business and civic blocks of Perth Amboy west of the downtown core, between Fayette Street at the top and Smith Street at the bottom, with Jefferson Street between them. The Central Railroad of New Jersey and the coal trestle of C. M. Peterson and Co., coal and wood, run vertically along the left edge. New Brunswick Avenue crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, lined with small shops, a creamery, a wholesale produce house, a bakery and a row of tenements, with East Avenue, Park Avenue and New Street entering it from the north. At the upper left are the H. Rosenthal handkerchief factory and a bakery lettered Simmens' Bakery, with a livery and carriage house. The W. J. Donnell lumber and mill work plant fills the block at the left between Fayette and Jefferson Streets. In the middle blocks are the Public Library, the Y.M.C.A. building (shown 'from plans'), Washington Hall and the Perth Amboy Cornice and Skylight Works. Below Jefferson Street the Custom House and Post Office, Grace Evangelical Lutheran Church, the Grand Theatre with its moving pictures, a telephone exchange, offices and stores line Smith Street. Maple Street and Madison Avenue run down the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose at the top right and a scale bar at the bottom.
notes: The Public Library and the Y.M.C.A. building are shown on the sheet; the Y.M.C.A. is marked 'from plans'.
The junction of New Brunswick Avenue and Fayette Street lies about 84 ft off the sheet and was not measured.
Civic/business blocks, New Brunswick Av diagonal. 50 ft.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 shows the central downtown of Perth Amboy where New Brunswick Avenue cuts diagonally across the grid from upper left to lower right between Madison Avenue at the left and State Street at the right. Fayette Street crosses the upper part, Jefferson Street the middle and Smith Street the bottom, with Division Street entering from the north and Hobart Street south of Smith Street. The triangular blocks along the avenue hold stores, banks, offices and halls, including the Auditorium, a theatre with a stage and scenery, a garage, a vacant building and The Ernst Ho. [hotel], a livery stable, a department store, a bank, an electrician and printing shop, a candy factory, a bakery and drug stores. Block 83 between Jefferson and Smith Streets holds the Marathon Hotel, a synagogue, bowling alleys, a moving picture house, a metal works and a furniture store. At the left, block 85 has the Den Danske Methodist Kirke, a garage and machine shop. Blocks across the sheet's edges (19, 20, 26, 28, 34) are blank. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with a compass rose at the left and a scale bar at the bottom.
notes: New Brunswick Avenue cuts diagonally across the sheet; Division Street, Fayette Street and New Brunswick Avenue meet at one place in the modern data.
The sheet carries a Danish Methodist church, lettered 'Den Danske Methodist Kirke'.
Downtown, New Brunswick Av diagonal. 50 ft.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows two rows of blocks in the old downtown of Perth Amboy, between State Street at the left and High Street at the right, with Fayette Street across the top, Jefferson Street through the middle and Smith Street along the bottom. Mechanic Street enters from the north at the top and King Street leaves to the south below Smith Street. The upper row, blocks 39 and 20, is mostly frame dwellings and sheds, a few brick stores along State Street, a laundry, carpenter shops, a paint shop, a leaded glass works and a copper smith, with the Simpson M.E. Church and its parsonage at the right. The lower row, block 40, is more closely built, with brick stores along Smith Street containing furniture, a five and ten cent store, a club room and lodge rooms, a pipe storage building, a garage, a barber and a hotel dining room, and a building lettered Packer Ho. at the corner of Smith and High Streets. The blocks outside the sheet, 20, 21, 27, 29, 34 and 35, are blank. A short piece of New Brunswick Avenue shows at the lower left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with a compass rose at the right and a scale bar at the lower right.
notes: The upper blocks are numbered 20 and 21 above Fayette Street and 39 and 40 below it, as lettered on the sheet.
Downtown blocks State to High, Fayette to Smith. 50 ft.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the waterfront edge of old downtown Perth Amboy, from High Street at the top down to Front Street and the Staten Island Sound shore at the bottom, between Smith Street on the left and Fayette Street on the right, with Jefferson Street running down the middle. Rector Street, Willock's Lane and Water Street cross the sheet from left to right. The upper blocks hold frame dwellings, small stores and a row of three-storey brick stores on the left, among them a drug store, a bakery and a restaurant, beside the Washington Hose and Chemical Company fire house. Across Jefferson Street a garage, stable, auto repair shop and a hollow tile works stand among the dwellings. Below Rector Street, a double block of flats and dwellings is bounded by Willock's Lane, with two brick buildings marked as stores or factories. The large block between Willock's Lane and Water Street is mostly open, with the ice cream factory, a few dwellings and, at the right, the foundry and machine shop of Patrick White and Sons, Founders and Machinists. South of Water Street, Front Street runs obliquely to the shore past the Ferry Hotel, the Perth Amboy Cigar Company store house, the Raritan Mercantile Company, Albert Killmeyer, Masons Supplies, and the long assembling and painting shop of the Ely-Norris Safe Company. Docks, a derrick and the irregular shoreline of Staten Island Sound fill the bottom edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north lies to the upper right, and carries a compass rose at the left. Water pipes are drawn in every street, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at several corners.
notes: Willock's Lane is not in the modern street data. Smith Street here is today's Smith Street, which runs down to the shore.
Sheet turned about 70 degrees: north is toward the upper right (compass rose at left).
High Street / Jefferson Street and Fayette Street / Front Street were not detected; six street junctions fit at 0.3 m RMSE.
Waterfront blocks High to Front, turned about +70. 50 ft.

sheet-30-1.description: The upper part of sheet 30 shows a district just north of Buckingham Avenue, between State Street on the left and High Street at the right edge. Miller Street runs down the left side, Mechanic Street crosses the right centre and Pearl Place runs across the middle. Buckingham Avenue closes the part at the bottom, where a heavy line separates it from the lower part of the sheet. At the top the Lehigh Valley Railroad (L.V.R.R.) sweeps across the sheet in a broad curve with several tracks, an L.V.R.R. office and, at upper left, State Street running diagonally across the track area. The blocks between Pearl Place and Buckingham Avenue are built with frame dwellings and flats, with warehouses and a grocery warehouse in the middle block, a tin shop, blacksmith and wood working shops, a printing office and hollow tile works along State Street, and at the left the McClellan Engine Company No. 3 fire house with a combination wagon and steam engine. East of Mechanic Street are rows of two-storey frame flats, a saloon and a beer storage building. The upper blocks between Pearl Place and the railroad are only partly built: a row of six dwellings, a vacant lot and open land. At the left, E. J. Dorsey and Sons, coal and ice, stands beside a 100 foot long shed. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees, with north to the upper left; the compass rose lies just below the dividing line on the lower part.
notes: High Street / Buckingham Avenue was left out of the fit: with it the part fits 7.57 px/ft and 3 m RMSE (that junction 4.5 m off); without it 7.81 px/ft and 0.8 m RMSE.
Part 1 is the upper area above the heavy line; part 2 is the lower area, further east along Buckingham Avenue.
Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 upper State to High (High St left out, spacing 8% short), 2 lower Hartford St, power station, Sound shore (anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-30-2.description: The lower part of sheet 30 lies below the heavy dividing line and shows the area east of the upper part along Buckingham Avenue, between High Street at the left edge and the shore of Staten Island Sound at the right. At the top the Lehigh Valley Railroad (L.V.R.R.) runs diagonally across the part with a footbridge or overpass at the head of Hartford Street, and a curved branch track leaves it down the left side. Hartford Street runs down the left centre with rows of frame dwellings on both sides, drawn in two narrow blocks numbered 209B and 210, with a saloon, a cobbler and several small shops among them; High Street forms the left edge. Buckingham Avenue runs across the bottom. The right two thirds of the part is a large open tract, numbered 209A, which belongs to the Public Service Electric Company, Perth Amboy Station, at the lower right. The station is a brick boiler house with coal bunkers above and an engine room and switchboard rooms, with an elevated steel frame conveyor that carries coal from the dock, a dock 320 feet long, and a small storage building. The text beside it describes the continuous operation, the hydrants and hose supplied from Staten Island Sound by underwriters' pumps, and the city water connection. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left, and carries the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Placed from one measured junction (Buckingham Avenue / Hartford Street) with a configured scale; low confidence. High Street / Buckingham Avenue agrees with it to 1.4 m.
Printed street names carry no suffix here: HARTFORD and HIGH.
Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 upper State to High (High St left out, spacing 8% short), 2 lower Hartford St, power station, Sound shore (anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the district of Perth Amboy west of the downtown, between Smith Street at the top and Gordon Street at the bottom, with Market Street crossing the middle. In the upper half Bertrand, Davidson, Watson Avenues and Prospect Street run down the sheet from left to right. The block between Bertrand and Davidson Avenues holds the Public Service Railway Company car barn, a power house marked not in operation with two generators, the Eagle Hose and Chemical Company No. 4 fire house, and a few frame buildings. Along Smith Street the block between Davidson and Watson Avenues has a row of brick stores with hollow tile works and a hollow tile shed, and behind them frame dwellings and tenements. East of Watson Avenue are frame dwellings, a bakery with an oven, the Amboy Whist and Dress Company with its light and power plant, a hay, feed and grain warehouse, and a water tower. A single track of the Raritan Terminal and Transportation Company runs diagonally from the upper middle across Market Street to the bottom edge. South of Market Street, Meade and Grant Streets bound a block of frame dwellings, while Olive and Walnut Streets bound lots of dwellings fronting Market Street and open ground below. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 20 degrees with north toward the upper left, and carries a compass rose at the left.
notes: Stockton Street is lettered at the top edge only, and is not in the modern street data as a street meeting this sheet.
Sheet 10's inset may share corners with this sheet (not checked).
Thirteen junctions fit at 1.1 m RMSE.
Smith/Market/Gordon, Bertrand to Walnut; Raritan Terminal track. 50 ft.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 shows Smith Street and Market Street in the west of Perth Amboy's downtown, with Prospect Street, Oak Street and Elm Street running between them. The upper half holds two large blocks between Smith Street and Market Street. On the left, between Prospect Street and Oak Street, brick and frame stores line Smith Street, and behind them are the Perth Amboy Bottling Company and its bottling works with storage sheds, a wood working shop, a cigar factory, frame dwellings, a vacant building, and at the foot of the block on Market Street the Raritan Bridge Hotel with a blue brick stage building. The block between Oak and Elm Streets has a department store and brick stores on Smith Street, an auto and carpet shop, a hollow tile works, and rows of frame dwellings, with a group of dwellings facing Market Street. East of Elm Street is a large lot, numbered 153, almost empty apart from a few dwellings and an auto building at its foot. South of Market Street only the front lots remain, with rows of frame dwellings facing Market Street, drawn between Walnut, Prospect and Oak Streets and east of Elm Street, and the lower half of the sheet is blank apart from the lettered streets and a scale bar. The double line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey lies at the right edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 20 degrees with north to the upper left.
notes: Prospect Street jogs across Market Street: it lies further left north of Market Street than south of it.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line at the right edge measured about 14 m from its modern line (rail warning only; no rail points were used).
Smith/Market, Prospect to Elm; lower half blank. 50 ft.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers the blocks around Smith Street, Market Street and Gordon Street in the centre of Perth Amboy, between the Central Railroad of New Jersey on the left and Madison Avenue on the right. Maple Street and McClellan Street cross the upper half, and 2nd Street and 1st Street the lower half. In the upper blocks, rows of two-storey frame dwellings and stores front Smith Street, among them a cigar factory, a saloon and a restaurant, with B. F. Rubright, coal and wood, and a stable block in the middle, and a block on the right that holds Proctor's Theatre, a garage with cement floor, a machine shop and the McClellan House. At the upper left lies the open ground of the railroad with a passenger depot and, below Market Street, a long freight house, a beer depot, a stone cutting shop, and the grain bins, lime and cement warehouse of R. G. Bolton and the grain mill of Hagaman. South of Market Street the blocks hold the Wilbert Blue Stone Company, the church lettered Deutsche Evangelische St. Paul's Kirche, a piano repair shop, a tin shop, and many frame dwellings, with brick flats at the lower right corner. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 20 degrees with north toward the upper left, and carries a compass rose at the top left.
notes: McClellan is Mc Clellan Street today; Madison Avenue is also lettered Woodbridge Av.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line measured 18 m from its modern line (rail warning only; no rail points were used).
Eleven junctions fit at 0.9 m RMSE.
C.R.R. of N.J. at left; Smith/Market/Gordon, Maple to Madison. 50 ft.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 shows the centre of old Perth Amboy, the blocks between Smith Street, Market Street and Gordon Street, with Madison Avenue at the left, Hobart Street and State Street in the middle and King Street and Kearney Avenue at the right. The upper middle block, bounded by Smith and Market Streets between Hobart and State Streets, holds the City Yard, with wagon yard, wagon shed, a bell tower, and the truck and engine company fire houses, and the Perth Amboy High School, a large brick school with a gymnasium wing, and Congregation Beth Mordecai. Along Smith Street brick stores, a bank and moving picture houses stand in a row, with Hotel Hobart at the left. East of State Street the Boynton Building, Hotel Central, the Perth Amboy Evening News plant, Ditmas Theater, Public School No. 7, and Our Saviour's Danish Lutheran Church line the blocks. The upper left block has the Hotel Madison, a hollow tile works and rows of frame dwellings. South of Market Street, Brighton Avenue and State Street bound a block with the First Swedish Congregational Church and frame dwellings, and the lower left and lower right blocks have frame dwellings, brick stores along Market Street and a few auto buildings. A slanting lot line divides the lower left block. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left, and has a compass rose in the City Yard.
notes: Kearney Avenue is Kearny Avenue today. Madison Avenue is also lettered Woodbridge Av.
Fourteen junctions fit at 0.8 m RMSE.
Downtown centre, Hobart to Kearney, City Yard, High School. 50 ft.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 shows the City Hall square at the heart of Perth Amboy, where High Street divides around an oval park of walks and flower beds at its crossing with Market Street. Smith Street runs across the top, Gordon Street across the bottom, with King Street and Kearney Avenue at the left and Rector Street at the right. The upper left block between King Street and High Street holds a row of brick stores along Smith Street with an insurance office, a garage and hollow tile works, the Amboy Works glass and bronze workers' building, N. J. Roofing Company, City Water Department with a meter shop and plumbing shop, City Water Department Store House, the Home for the Aged and the Eagle A. C. building. The upper right block has a row of stores along Smith Street with the Island Hotel at the corner, a steam laundry, a livery and a wagon shed, and, at its lower end, City Hall and the Police Station. Below Market Street the lower right block holds the First Presbyterian Church, stuccoed, with a chapel, and the Warren House, with frame dwellings and flats; the lower left block has frame dwellings in the Kearney Avenue frontage and open lots to High Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left and a compass rose at the left.
notes: Kearney Avenue is Kearny Avenue today.
High Street and Market Street meet twice at the oval park (two modern nodes 59 m apart); neither was detected and neither was used.
Eight junctions fit at 0.6 m RMSE.
City Hall square (oval park), King to Rector. 50 ft.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 lies on the Staten Island Sound waterfront at the east end of the old city, between Smith Street at the top and Gordon Street at the bottom, and between Rector Street on the left and the shore on the right. Water Street and Front Street run down the sheet, Front Street following the edge of the bulkhead and Market Street crossing the middle. The blocks on the left, between Rector and Water Streets, are mostly dwellings, flats and small stores, with a hotel, sheds and stables near Smith Street. Between Smith and Market Streets east of Water Street the ground is occupied by the Hartmanns Hotel, the Staten Island Rapid Transit ferry to Tottenville, the New York and New Jersey Steamboat Company freight house and the shops of Schantz and Eckert, a machine shop, pattern shop and iron foundry with cupolas and a core oven, built of steel frame and hollow tile. Beyond them Gray Bros. Marine Railways, with a timber saw mill, extends into the water on timber ways. South of Market Street the blocks are thinly built, with a few dwellings, a larger pink-coloured building on Water Street, and boat houses and the Raritan Point Club on piers at the foot of Gordon Street. The shore, piers, slips and ferry landing are drawn in blue and have since been rebuilt. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass rose over the water and the scale bar at the foot. Adjoining sheets 29, 35, 43 and 44 are numbered at the edges.
notes: The shoreline, piers, slips and ferry landing have been rebuilt; only the street junctions were used for control.
Smith Street / Rector Street, at the top left corner, was not detected; seven junctions were used.
Staten Island Sound waterfront, Smith to Gordon. 50 ft.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers a district of Perth Amboy south of the Central Railroad's right of way, between Gordon Street at the top and the blocks south of Paterson Street at the bottom. The railroad tracks run down the left edge of the sheet, with 2nd Street immediately to their right, then a very large block numbered 69 that is mostly open ground with a storage shed and a scattering of small buildings. 1st Street forms the next boundary, and the narrow blocks along its east side, numbered 68 and 60, are closely built with dwellings and stores up to Madison Avenue, also lettered Woodbridge Avenue, on the right edge. Beside the tracks are an ice house, E. J. Dorsey and Sons coal and ice, Herman Ellis, junk dealer, with a rubber, metals and rags store and a water tower, and P. Larsen's coal yard. East of 1st Street, near Gordon Street, stand Otto E. Hansen's gas log manufactory and clay working shop, a Negro Baptist church, a garage, a hollow tile works and a packing and storage building, and a junk yard is marked further south. Below Paterson Street the blocks are narrower, with dwellings facing 1st Street and Madison Avenue and a cement works. The sheet is at 50 feet to an inch, with a compass rose and scale bar at the lower left. Sheets 33, 38, 39 and 48 are numbered at the edges.
notes: Paterson Street is Patterson Street today; 1st Street and 2nd Street are First Street and Second Street in OpenStreetMap; Madison Avenue is also lettered Woodbridge Avenue.
The Central Railroad tracks along the left edge lie about 16 m from the modern North Jersey Coast Line, measured against the street fit; no rail points were used for control.
Gordon/Paterson, 2nd/1st/Madison; railroad at left edge drawn 16 m off. 50 ft.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 shows the river end of the same district as sheet 37, from the lower part of its blocks down to the Raritan River. Lewis Street crosses the middle of the sheet, with 2nd Street, 1st Street and Madison Avenue (also lettered Woodbridge Avenue) running down to the water. The upper part, above Lewis Street, repeats blocks 59 and 60 of sheet 37 with dwellings and a few brick buildings between 2nd Street and Madison Avenue. Below Lewis Street the streets are drawn as bare lines to the bulkhead; the block between 2nd and 1st Streets, numbered 56, is empty, and the narrow block along the east side of 1st Street and Madison Avenue holds only a few dwellings on the Madison Avenue frontage. A structural iron works and a printing ink company stand beside the railroad tracks at the left edge, where several tracks run down the sheet and out to the river. The shoreline, drawn as a heavy curved line with the street ends projecting as bulkheads, runs across the lower part of the sheet and the Raritan River fills the foot. A compass rose is placed in the water at lower left and the scale bar is at the bottom centre. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch. Sheets 37, 39, 40, 48, 56 and 57 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Only Lewis Street junctions were available, so the part rests on a three-point helmert and is low confidence; the streets south of Lewis Street end in the river, where the modern Sadowski Parkway replaced them.
Lewis Street, First Street and Second Street are as in OpenStreetMap.
Lewis Street to Raritan River; only Lewis junctions (helmert, low). 50 ft.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers a block-and-a-half wide strip of dwellings between Gordon Street at the top and the area below Paterson Street, from Madison Avenue (also lettered Woodbridge Avenue) on the left to State Street on the right, with Brighton Avenue in the middle. The sheet is closely built with frame dwellings, mostly two storeys, on narrow lots along the avenues. Several pink-coloured brick buildings stand on the Madison Avenue frontage between Gordon and Paterson Streets, a furniture storage building and a small group of blue-coloured stable or shop buildings sit east of Brighton Avenue, and Public School No. 7 stands on a large lot at the corner of Paterson Street and Madison Avenue. Brighton Avenue, a narrower street, runs through to Paterson Street and beyond, where Catalpa Avenue branches off at an angle and carries rows of dwellings and a few shops along it at the lower right. Harrison Place appears at the right edge. The blocks are numbered 65 to 67 above Paterson Street and 61 and 63 below it. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch, with the compass rose at the upper left and the scale bar at the foot. Adjoining sheets 34, 37, 40 and 41 are named in the margins.
notes: Paterson Street is Patterson Street today; Catalpa Avenue is Capalta Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Madison Avenue is also lettered Woodbridge Avenue.
Gordon/Paterson, Madison/Brighton/State. 50 ft.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 lies between Lewis Street and the Raritan River, from Madison Avenue (also lettered Woodbridge Avenue) at the left to State Street on the right, with Brighton Avenue and the diagonal Catalpa Avenue between. Above Lewis Street the large block 61 at the upper left is almost empty, a narrow wedge block 62 lies between Brighton and Catalpa Avenues, and block 63 east of Catalpa Avenue holds rows of dwellings, several of them pink-coloured brick. Below Lewis Street, between Madison and Brighton Avenues, stand two rows of brick dwellings in groups of six and three, and the lower part of the block, block 54, is open ground used by the Gregory Wrecking and Contracting Company. The wedge-shaped blocks 52 and 53 between Catalpa Avenue and State Street carry a few dwellings and sheds, and a small boat or wharf building stands at the foot of State Street on a pier. The river bank runs across the lower part of the sheet as a heavy curved line with a blue tint, and the Raritan River is lettered in the water. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch, with a compass rose at upper right and the scale bar at the foot. Sheets 38, 39, 41 and 42 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Catalpa Avenue is Capalta Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Only Lewis Street junctions were available, so the part rests on a four-point helmert and is low confidence.
Lewis Street to Raritan River, Madison to State; helmert (low). 50 ft.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 covers two rows of blocks of dwellings between Gordon Street at the top and the area south of Paterson Street, from State Street on the left to High Street on the right, with Kearney Avenue between them and Harrison Place crossing the middle. The blocks, numbered 45 to 48, are laid out with long narrow lots and are almost entirely residential: frame dwellings, mostly two storeys, with sheds and stables in the yards and a few pink-coloured brick buildings. The lower block west of Kearney Avenue includes a larger brick building with a long rear wing and a smaller one beside it, and the lots along the east side of Kearney Avenue are filled with a nearly continuous line of small dwellings. Paterson Street appears as a short stub at the left edge, and Woodruff Place is lettered at the right edge near the bottom. The area below the lowest blocks is open ground. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch, with a compass rose at the left edge and the scale bar and Princeton map division stamp at the foot. Adjoining sheets 34, 35, 39, 42 and 43 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Kearney Avenue is Kearny Avenue today and Paterson Street is Patterson Street; Harrison Place is as in OpenStreetMap.
Gordon/Harrison Place, State/Kearney/High. 50 ft.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 is the southeast corner of this part of the city, running from Lewis Street, which crosses the sheet at the top, down to the Raritan River. Streets are drawn at an angle: State Street on the left, then Wisteria Street, Linden Street and High Street on the right, with Kearney Avenue entering from the north. The blocks above Lewis Street are lightly built with dwellings and outbuildings. Below it the blocks between State Street and Linden Street are mostly open ground with a few dwellings, but along Linden Street stand the works of the Perth Amboy Gas Light Company: a coal shed, pipe storage, gasometers of 20,000 and 80,000 cubic feet, a purifying house, engine house and retort house. East of Linden Street, the Ashland Emery and Corundum Company plant is shown not in operation, with crushers, an engine house, a water tank and a large vacant works, and a caretaker lives at 73 Linden Street. A long pier and wharf with a slip run out at the foot of Linden and High Streets into the river. The drawing is at 50 feet to an inch, with the compass rose at upper right and the scale bar at the foot. Sheets 40, 41, 43 and 44 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Kearney Avenue is Kearny Avenue today; Lewis Street, Linden Street and Wisteria Street are as in OpenStreetMap.
The Lewis Street junctions lie nearly on one line; the part is placed by a helmert from them and one cross street (High Street and Woodruff Place) and is medium to low confidence.
Lewis Street to the river, State/Wisteria/Linden/High; gas works. 50 ft.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 shows a strip of Perth Amboy's waterfront district along Staten Island Sound, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees from the page edges. High Street runs down the left margin, Rector Street divides the sheet near its middle and Water Street lies to the right of it, with Front Street reaching the shore at the top right corner. Gordon Street crosses the top of the sheet and Woodruff Place closes the main map at the bottom, below which a framed blank box holds the scale bar. The blocks between High and Rector Streets are built up with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, most with auto sheds, and at the upper end the D. McClymont greenhouses, a wagon shed, the old green house and the stuccoed St. Peter's Parish Hall with a frame top. Between Rector and Water Streets the upper half is occupied by the burying ground of St. Peter's Protestant Episcopal Church, lettered Cemetery, with the church, a 110 foot spire, shown in the middle; the lower half is lined with dwellings, several of hollow tile, and open lots. East of Water Street dwellings and outbuildings stand above a top-of-bank line, a footpath leads to the shore, and a bath house, a boat house and a private dock on piles project into the Sound. The compass rose and the lettering Staten Island Sound lie over the water on the right.
notes: The sheet is turned about 21 degrees, with north toward the upper left.
Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 35, 36, 41, 42 and 44; the lower left box is blank.
Gordon and Front Streets also appear in the inset of sheet 44 at the same corner.
Waterfront Gordon/Water/Rector/High, St Peter's cemetery. 50 ft.

sheet-44-1.description: This is the main map of sheet 44, the southern end of the waterfront district of Perth Amboy where High Street and Water Street converge on the Raritan River. Woodruff Place runs across the top and Lewis Street crosses the upper third of the sheet; Rector Street runs down between them, High Street slants down the left side towards the river, and Water Street runs diagonally from the upper right to the bottom, where the two streets meet at the shore. The block between Woodruff Place and Lewis Street west of Rector Street holds frame dwellings, auto houses and a large hollow tile building, with a small blue-coloured structure in the centre of the block.
