The triangular block between High Street, Lewis Street and Water Street contains rows of two and two and a half storey dwellings facing High Street, larger houses and outbuildings facing Water Street, a greenhouse and a large pink dwelling near the southern apex. North of Lewis Street, east of Rector Street, a stuccoed house and other residences stand on the block extending to Water Street. East of Water Street the sheet shows the river and Sound with irregular private docks on piles and the Raritan River lettered across the bottom. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at the left edge. The scale is 50 feet to an inch, with the compass rose at the right and the sheet turned about 21 degrees. An inset occupies the bottom right corner (part 2).
notes: Water Street is drawn with a very wide diagonal course and meets the river shore beyond the point where High Street ends; the High Street and Water Street junction near the bottom could not be measured from the drawn lines.
Adjoining sheets are numbered 42 and 43 in the margins.
Two parts: 1 main (High/Water at the Raritan); 2 inset Front/Gordon, Hampton Kerosene Carburetor (anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-44-2.description: This inset in the bottom right corner of sheet 44 is bounded by a heavy double rule and continues the waterfront at the top right corner of sheet 43. It shows Front Street running down the left side and Gordon Street crossing near the top, with a six-inch water pipe in each. Between them and the shore stands the works of The Hampton Kerosene Carburetor Co., Inc.: a frame dwelling and shed at the left, a brick machine shop with an office and a roof full of skylights, and a lettered note on its night watchman, magneto clock stations, half-hourly rounds, steam heat, electric power and lights, and chemical and fire pails. A club house, Club No. 2, used in summer as an oyster depot in winter stands on a pier at the right. Private docks on piles, one marked Dock, run out into Staten Island Sound along the right and bottom edges. The inset is drawn at the same 50 feet to an inch and at the same angle as the main part, with a sheet 36 block number at the top and a 43 block number on the left.
notes: Placed from a single hand-picked point at the Front Street and Gordon Street junction, with scale and rotation taken from sheet 43; low confidence.
The inset repeats ground drawn on the corner of sheet 43 and sheet 36.
Two parts: 1 main (High/Water at the Raritan); 2 inset Front/Gordon, Hampton Kerosene Carburetor (anchored, low). 50 ft.

sheet-45-1.description: Sheet 45 covers the industrial waterfront of Perth Amboy along the Raritan River and Meadow Creek, east of the river and west of the railroad. The upper right of the sheet is occupied by the Chesebrough Manufacturing Co., Vaseline Factory: two large pink warehouses (No. 1 and No. 2, finished goods), a long mill-construction building housing unfinished goods, bottling and compounding departments, a canning floor, tank houses, an inclined conveyor, a loading shed and a fire-proof construction building, with sprinkler risers and hydrants lettered on each. A long note at the left gives the company's watchmen, sprinkler and fire-fighting arrangements. Below Meadow Creek, which crosses the middle of the sheet, are the Marcy Stove Repair Co. foundry, pattern storage, cupola, machine and pattern shop, flask storage, coal and coke bins and a hollow-tile warehouse, then a large pink works and yellow sheds at the bottom left. The Raritan River widens across the left of the sheet, and a reservoir with a capacity of 600,000 gallons lies at the bottom. The right edge carries the railroad, a trolley ferry track on a wooden trestle leading to the bridge to South Amboy, and Grant Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 70 degrees so that north points to the upper right, with the compass rose at the top. An inset at the upper left (part 2) shows a dock on the river.
notes: Placed from one point on the railroad strip at the Grant Street junction, measured on sheet 46; low confidence, with scale and rotation taken from sheet 46.
The sheet shows no other street junction. Adjoining sheets are numbered 0, 46 and 48 in the margins.
A trolley ferry track on a wooden trestle and the wooden bridge to South Amboy run across the top right.
Chesebrough Vaseline works, Marcy Stove; part 1 anchored on a point carried from sheet 46 (low); part 2 inset dock on the Raritan, not placed. 50 ft.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: dock on the Raritan River with warehouse (no street junction or shared feature).

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 lies in the northern part of Perth Amboy near the Raritan River and Meadow Creek, with the page turned about 70 degrees so that the streets run across the page. The left third is occupied by the Chesebrough Manufacturing Co. Vaseline Works: a filter house, stock room and pump rooms of 1904, a clay retort house, a machine shop, a naphtha wash plant, oil storage tanks numbered 34 to 39, a coal pile, a fan house and electric shop, a still yard with stills and tanks, and at the bottom left the fireproof bottling building of 1912 with a long note on watchmen and sprinklers. Meadow Creek crosses the works with its top of bank lines. A railroad and a wooden trestle for the trolley line, with a wooden bridge to South Amboy, run along the left and top left edges. To the right of Paterson Street the sheet shows the residential blocks laid out between Sheridan, Sherman, Meade and Grant Streets, crossed by Gordon Street and Colfax Street: frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys on narrow lots, a slack cooperage shop and tight cooperage, a bag storage building, tenements and, along the lower right, a Raritan Terminal and Transportation Co. line. The streets are 60 feet wide with six and twenty-four inch water pipes. The scale is 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets 45, 47 and 31 are numbered in the margins.
notes: The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right, about 70 degrees from the page vertical.
A line of the Raritan Terminal and Transportation Co. crosses the bottom right corner.
Streets here are drawn 60 feet wide.
Turned +70; Chesebrough works, Sheridan/Sherman/Meade/Grant. 50 ft.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 shows a district of Perth Amboy between Smith Street at the top, Market Street across the middle and Gordon Street at the bottom, with the street grid turned about 20 degrees from the page edges. Grace, Goodwin and Bertrand Avenue run down the upper half, and Sheridan, Sherman and Meade Streets run down the lower half, offset to the right of the upper streets. The upper blocks are densely built with frame dwellings, tenements, hollow tile stores and sheds, a wagon house and wagon sheds, and at the corner of Smith Street and Bertrand Avenue the Hotel Remington with an office and a saloon. Along Sheridan Street are an auto and wagon repair shop and a trucking premises with a wagon shed in a large pink building. Along Meade Street the lots are filled with long rows of two and two and a half storey dwellings, with stores at the Market Street end. At the left edge an open area is cut by a ragged line, west of which the sheet is blank, and a railroad curves in at the lower left. Kirkland Place and Gifford Street come down from the top margin, where only their ends are shown. Six, twelve, sixteen and twenty-four inch water pipes run in the streets, which are marked 50 and 66 feet wide. The scale is 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets 23, 24, 31, 46 and 50 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Sheridan, Sherman and Meade are offset from Grace, Goodwin and Bertrand Avenue across Market Street; Goodwin and Sherman are about 7 m apart.
The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left, about 20 degrees from the page vertical.
Smith/Market/Gordon, Grace to Bertrand. 50 ft.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 shows the Raritan Copper Works, a copper refining plant on the south bank of the Raritan River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch (a bar at the bottom reads 100 ft to one inch). The page is turned about 20 degrees so that north points to the upper left. Two long pink tank houses (No. 1 and No. 2) of mill construction with steel trusses and raised roofs dominate the centre, with the power house, silver house, slimes room, sulphate house, selenium plant, foundry, machine shop, recovering plant, locomotive house, store house, coal house, copper store house, sample house, charcoal shed and the Anaconda Laboratory around them. Furnace houses No. 1 and No. 2 are iron buildings, not sprinklered. Tracks on a trestle serve the power house. A reservoir of 600,000 gallons lies at the left. A note records the 1,800 hands by day, 200 by night, watchmen, magneto clocks, automatic sprinklers, hydrants and the plant's own fire department; the plant is marked Admission Refused, diagram from plans. A railroad runs across the top of the sheet with several tracks, and Grant Street ends at it from the north. The Raritan River forms the left and bottom edge, with a dock and pump house at the lower left and a railroad Iron Bridge at the bottom right.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point at the Grant Street and railroad junction, shared with sheets 45 and 46; scale 100 ft to an inch from the sheet; low confidence.
The works are drawn from plans because admission was refused.
Adjoining sheets are numbered 45 and 38 in the margins.
Raritan Copper Works, 100 ft; anchored on a point carried from sheet 46 (low).

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 shows the Perth Amboy plant of the National Fire Proofing Company, manufacturers of hollow brick and tile, on the south shore of the Raritan River at the west end of the city, with a strip of the adjoining Pardee Works along the right edge. The left and centre of the sheet belong to the National plant: a brick factory and steam dry houses with their boiler and steam lines, a large frame-covered continuous kiln drawn as an oval, a field of round kilns numbered 21 to 34, further single kilns, a blower house, a machine shop, an office, storage sheds, thermometer houses and a locomotive house, all laid out in open ground crossed by railroad sidings. A sawdust pile and a coal pile are marked at the upper left, and a large pond or stockpile outline is drawn beside the tracks. The printed legend describes the plant's watchman service, steam heat and power, electric lighting and the connection of the yard to the city water works with a hose cart. At the lower left the Raritan River shows as a blue band with an open dock on piles. At the right the sheet continues onto the C. Pardee Works tile department: kiln rooms, a glazing kiln room, shipping and stock rooms, clay bins, slip rooms, a floor tile room, storage sheds, an iron storage shed, a blacksmith shop and a gate shop, with Fox Hill Road running off the top right, and Rolling Mill No. 2 at the lower right. A property line crosses the middle of the sheet and several railroad branches converge on the plant. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and has no street junctions; the right margin repeats the left edge of sheet 50.
notes: Fox Hill Road is not in the modern OpenStreetMap data used here.
The sheet has no street intersection; it is placed from hydrants and building corners that sheet 50 repeats along its left edge.
The compass rose on this sheet is turned about 9 degrees from the one on sheet 50, and the sheet is drawn turned by the same amount.
National Fire Proofing Co. plant and Pardee tile dept; no junctions, placed from 5 points carried from sheet 50 (low). 50 ft.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 continues the C. Pardee Works at the west end of Perth Amboy, covering its steel department, with part of the street grid appearing at the upper right. Along the left side are Rolling Mill No. 1 (an iron building), a power house, a machine shop, gas producers, a stock house and a long Shafting Department No. 1, beside Shafting Department No. 2, which was not in operation in December 1913 and is built of hollow tile and reinforced concrete with a skylighted roof. Lower down are the electric generator house, a storage house, the long Blooming Mill House of iron construction, and the Open Hearth Furnace House with its gas producers beside a railroad siding on the right. Many railroad tracks fan out across the sheet from the upper left, curve down past the shafting departments and cross Market Street on their way east. At the upper right Herbert Street, drawn 60 feet wide, runs up the page and meets Market Street at an angle, with a gate house on the corner and a block numbered 144 containing a few small buildings. Water pipes of 6, 12 and 16 inches are drawn across the yard. The Fresh Water Pond, with its pumps, lies at the bottom left and the legend describes the works' night watchmen, hose and fire equipment. A bottom margin notes no exposures. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned about 13 degrees from sheet 49.
notes: Placed from the single junction of Herbert Street and Market Street; the rotation is set from the drawn direction of Market Street, which sheet 47 also draws.
The compass rose on this sheet points about 16 degrees left of the sheet's top, which does not match the street grid; the streets were trusted instead.
Herbert Street and Market Street keep their names today; Market Street east of here appears on sheet 47.
Pardee Works steel dept; one junction (Herbert/Market) plus a hand-made derived point (low). 50 ft.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 shows a mostly undeveloped part of Perth Amboy near Amboy Avenue, drawn as a grid of platted blocks with sparse building. Alpine, Keene, Grove and Lawrence Streets run down the page and are crossed by Chester Street at the top, Spring Street across the upper middle and Francis Street across the lower middle. At the right, beyond Lawrence Street, Birch, Pine and Wolff Streets run to the right edge, with smaller blocks numbered 324 M, N and O. Each block is divided into long narrow lots, and the blocks are numbered with a letter and a number such as 2A to 7A at left and 324 C to J in the middle. Most of the buildings are small frame dwellings, with a few flats, a saloon and several hollow tile structures marked in pink, concentrated near Spring Street, along Lawrence Street and in the lower right corner. Water mains of 6 inches are drawn in Francis Street and elsewhere with hydrants shown by dots, and a fire alarm box stands at the corner of Francis and Lawrence Streets. Street widths of 50 feet are marked on most streets and 47 feet on Wolff. A scale bar sits on Francis Street, and a compass rose at the lower right shows the sheet turned about 62 degrees from north. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Many of these streets no longer exist in the same form, although the names survive on the modern map.
notes: Thirteen junctions were detected automatically and fit to 0.5 m.
The sheet is turned about 65 degrees from north, so the modern street grid runs obliquely across it.
Alpine/Keene/Grove/Lawrence grid, turned about +65. 50 ft.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers a narrow wedge of Perth Amboy running south from Amboy Avenue, where the street pattern fans out from a point on Amboy Avenue and is drawn bent in several places. At the top, Amboy Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right and the streets Wagner Avenue, Ashley, Thomas and Inslee run down the page from it, diverging as they go. Laura crosses between Ashley and Thomas near the top, Anton crosses between Thomas and Inslee in the middle, and Pine runs across the lower part of the sheet, ending at Garretson Avenue at the lower right. The blocks are long, narrow and finely divided into lots, many with no buildings, and are numbered with a letter and a number such as 1A to 8A on the left and 326 C, D and E and 384 on the right. Buildings are mostly small frame dwellings with a few flats and hollow tile structures drawn in pink; at the top there are some factories and shops along Amboy Avenue and a saloon and tenements, and a saloon, stucco dwellings and shops along the lower right edge of Inslee Street. Street widths between 25 and 55 feet are marked, a water main of 6 inches and 8 inches is drawn, and hydrants appear at several corners. A compass rose at the upper right shows the sheet turned about 70 degrees from north, and a scale bar is at the bottom right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Laura survives as Laura Place and Garretson Avenue as Garretson Avenue in the modern data.
OpenStreetMap carries two nodes for Garretson Avenue and Pine Street 26 m apart; the sheet draws one junction, so the southern node was left out.
The modern Anton Street and Thomas Street node is about 4 m from where the sheet draws it and was left out of the fit.
Amboy Av wedge (Wagner/Ashley/Thomas/Inslee); doubled Garretson/Pine node excluded. 50 ft.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about a quarter circle, so that north lies to the right of the page and the Staten Island Sound shore runs along the lower left. It covers the works of the United Lead Co. and, on the left, the planing mill and lumber yard of the Perth Amboy Lumber Co., north of the city of Perth Amboy near Maurer. No street is lettered on the sheet. The Lumber Co. holds the left third: lumber sheds, piles and an office beside a pair of Lehigh Valley Railroad sidings, with a planing mill, engine room and saw-filing room at the water's edge and an open dock on piles running out into the sound. The centre is taken by two large Stack House buildings and the fireproof white lead mill built in 1906, with casting and wall houses, joined by an elevated trolley, a barrel shed and board fence along the yard. On the right are the U.S. Cartridge Co.'s reinforced concrete factory built in 1910, the Hoyt Metal Co. office and store house, a laboratory, the shot tower building (built 1907, tower 160 feet), the Mixed Metal Building, the Blue Lead Department with its pipe-making, motor and trap departments, a machine shop and carpenter shop, a power house with coal bin and chimney, a gross house and several stores. Railroad tracks curve across the lower part of the sheet and a track on trestle runs south from the coal bin. Water pipes and hydrants are shown. The right edge repeats the buildings drawn on sheet 54, to which it joins. Two block numbers (344, 345) are printed.
notes: No street is lettered; the part was placed from building corners it shares with sheet 54, not from street junctions.
The drawn compass points north to the right and about 11 degrees from the north the placement gives (as on sheet 54).
United Lead Co. works and Perth Amboy Lumber Co. at Maurer, turned north-right; placed from 5 building corners carried from sheet 54 (low). 50 ft.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies to the right of the page. It shows the plant of the American Smelting & Refining Co. at Maurer, north of the city of Perth Amboy, between State Street, which crosses the top of the sheet on a diagonal, and Staten Island Sound to the east (the sheet notes about 450 feet to the sound from the Roaster Building). The works fill the centre and left: the Lead Refinery with a long flue and chimney, the Parting Plant, the Copper Refinery Tank House, the Blue Vitriol House and Blue Vitriol Storage House, the Power House, the Castings building, the Roaster Building, Blast Furnace, Ore Shed, Sampling Mill, machine and black smith shops, stores and ware houses, many numbered. A cooling pond lies north of the tank house and an acid plant with lead chambers and iron tanks stands near State Street. A fan of railroad tracks and sidings enters from the upper left, with a track on trestle through the middle of the plant, and board fences enclose the grounds. At the upper right a laboratory and an office stand outside the fence. At the right edge, beyond the works, two short streets, Reo Street and Elmo Street, carry a few dwellings, with a larger house and a lot line to the south. The adjoining sheets are numbered 53, 55, 56, 57 and 58. A water-works note, a work-hours note and the scale bar fill the lower right. The words 'Admission Refused - Diagram from Plans' are printed across the plant.
notes: The part is anchored on one hand-picked point (the unnamed street opening on State Street at the top of the sheet, taken as Garretson Avenue) with scale and rotation from State Street; low confidence.
The drawn compass points north to the right and about 14 degrees away from the rotation the placement gives (the compass is probably magnetic).
Reo Street and Elmo Street are not in the modern street data.
American Smelting & Refining Co. at Maurer, State St along the top, turned north-right; anchored on Garretson Av / State St (unnamed street on the sheet; low). 100 ft.

sheet-58-1.description: Sheet 58, part 1, is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows State Street running down the right side of the page, between Perth Amboy and Maurer. The Central Railroad of New Jersey, a multiple-track line labelled 'C. R. R. of N. J.', runs parallel to it on the left with a curved spur turning off to the west. Between the railroad and State Street an unnamed 50 foot street, labelled 'Not Named' and carrying a 6 inch water pipe, runs west from State Street. North of it lies a block with a hollow tile factory, not in operation; south of it are small dwellings and outbuildings, and the Amboy Inn Hotel (Jos. Gadek, proprietor), an L-shaped building with dining room and saloon. House numbers in the 800s are written along State Street, whose width is marked as 66 feet. West of the railroad stands the factory of The American Encaustic Tiling Co. Ltd. (wall and floor tiles), with biscuit kiln, glaze, drying, pressing, mill and machine departments, a mosaic department building and a fenced yard served by a railroad spur. The upper left of the sheet is blank. The lower left corner holds a separate heavy-ruled inset (Fords Porcelain Works Plant No. 1) which is not part of this mask. Block numbers 334, 348 and 349 are printed, and sheet 54 adjoins on the right.
notes: The unnamed street printed 'Not Named' is taken as Garretson Avenue, which ends about 60 m west of State Street in the modern data.
The part is anchored on one hand-picked point at that junction with scale from the atlas and rotation from State Street; low confidence.
State Street with C.R.R. of N.J., American Encaustic Tiling Co., Amboy Inn; part 1 anchored on Garretson / State (low); part 2 inset Fords Porcelain Works, not placed. 50 ft.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Fords Porcelain Works Plant No. 1, 4 miles W of City Hall (crossing of Old Kings Highway and L.V.R.R. not identified in modern data; needs a located crossing near Fords, or parcel corners).

sheet-60-1.description: The upper part of sheet 60 shows the north end of Perth Amboy along Pulaski Avenue, from State Street at the left to Parker Street at the right. Pulaski Avenue crosses the part from left to right with a slight bend east of Central Place; Valley Place, Central Place and Gadek Place run up from it into the blocks numbered 311A to 311D, which are laid out in narrow house lots and partly built with two- and three-storey frame dwellings, flats and saloons, with a few brick-veneered buildings and outbuildings in the rear yards. Below Pulaski Avenue the blocks numbered 340 and 341 are almost empty apart from a few dwellings and an auto shed near Parker Street at the right. State Street crosses the left side of the part diagonally, and the Pennsylvania Railroad (marked P. R. R.) runs parallel to it further left. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes are drawn along Pulaski Avenue, Gadek Place, Parker Street and State Street, with a hydrant at State Street. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 11 degrees from the downtown sheets so that Pulaski Avenue runs across the page. A heavy line with a bend in the middle separates it from the lower part of the sheet, an inset of the National Fire Proofing Company's Standard Plant on the Raritan River, which lies elsewhere on the ground.
notes: Placed from five junctions along Pulaski Avenue only; the fit rests on one street and is weak across it.
The lower part of the sheet (National Fire Proofing Co. Standard Plant) was not placed.

Two parts divided by a bent heavy line: part 1 (top) Pulaski Av from State St to Parker St, Valley Pl, Central Pl, Gadek Pl, rotation about -9; part 2 (bottom) National Fire Proofing Co. Standard Plant on the Raritan River (not placed). 50 ft.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: National Fire Proofing Co. Standard Plant, Raritan north shore (no street junction; Raritan North Shore R.R. and shoreline not in modern data; needs step 6b; no placed neighbour).
